paper.title: Predicting thermodynamic stability of inorganic compounds using ensemble machine learning based on electron configuration
paper.research_summary: This paper proposes an ensemble machine learning framework—Electron Configuration models with Stacked Generalization (ECSG)—to predict the thermodynamic stability of inorganic compounds. ECSG integrates three base-level models grounded in distinct domain knowledge: electron configuration (via ECCNN), atomic properties (Magpie), and interatomic interactions (Roost). The framework achieves high predictive accuracy (AUC = 0.988 on JARVIS) and exceptional sample efficiency (requiring only 1/7 the data of existing models). It is validated across multiple databases (MP, OQMD, JARVIS), unknown composition spaces (perovskite halides, Li-containing oxides, transition metal oxides), and applied in two case studies: discovery of 2D wide bandgap semiconductors and double perovskite oxides—both confirmed via first-principles calculations.

task.task_name_raw: Predicting thermodynamic stability of inorganic compounds
task.objective: Accurately predict whether an inorganic compound is thermodynamically stable (i.e., has negative decomposition energy ΔHd)
constraints: compounds must be inorganic crystalline solids
input_requirements: atomic properties (e.g., atomic number, radius, electronegativity)

evidence.text: Predicting thermodynamic stability of inorganic compounds using ensemble machine learning based on electron configuration

The thermodynamic stability of materials is typically represented by the decomposition energy (ΔHd)6, which is defined as the total energy difference between a given compound and competing compounds in a specific chemical space.
Compounds with a ΔHd below 0 meV/atom were considered stable and are labeled accordingly.

stages.stage_name_raw: Collecting DFT-computed stability data from public materials databases
stages.stage_goal: Acquire large-scale, experimentally validated or DFT-calculated thermodynamic stability labels for inorganic compounds

evidence.text: In this work, we compared the performance of various models in predicting the stability of inorganic compounds on three large DFT-computed datasets, MP, OQMD, and JARVIS.

Before using these databases, data preprocessing was required. After excluding noble gas and radioactive elements, the MP database contained 85,014 compounds with information on thermodynamic properties such as formation energy.
We extracted the composition and stability information of the materials from the entire C2DB database and trained a model to predict the thermodynamic stability of 2D materials.

stages.stage_goal: Transform raw chemical formulas into structured inputs suitable for ML models—including element-fraction vectors, statistical atomic features, graph representations, and electron configuration matrices

evidence.text: The input of ECCNN is a matrix with shape of 118 × 168 × 8, which is encoded by the EC of materials.

The construction of the features for ECCNN is illustrated in Fig. 8. The first step involves identifying the categories of elements in the compound... To represent the number of electrons in each subshell, one-hot encoding is employed...

Magpie incorporates chemical information for each element into its material representations using features such as atomic electronegativity, atomic radii, and elemental group. This results in a total of 132 features, generated using the Matminer62, and the model is trained using XGBoost.

stages.stage_name_raw: Deriving stability labels from decomposition energy (ΔHd) via convex hull analysis
stages.stage_goal: Compute binary stability labels by determining whether each compound lies on the convex hull of its elemental phase diagram
stage_output: binary labels: stable (ΔHd < 0 meV/atom) or unstable

evidence.text: The thermodynamic stability of materials is typically represented by the decomposition energy (ΔHd)6, which is defined as the total energy difference between a given compound and competing compounds in a specific chemical space. For detailed definitions of ΔHd, see Supplementary Note 1. This metric is ascertained by constructing a convex hull utilizing the formation energies of compounds and all pertinent materials within the same phase diagram7.
Compounds with a ΔHd below 0 meV/atom were considered stable and are labeled accordingly.

stages.stage_name_raw: Training base-level models (ECCNN, Magpie, Roost) and meta-level model (MLR) via stacked generalization
stages.stage_goal: Train three complementary base models on compositional inputs, then train a meta-level linear regressor to combine their outputs into a super learner (ECSG)

evidence.text: We utilized a highly effective ensemble technique called SG to combine the predictions from these individual models for forecasting the thermodynamic stability of materials. This ensemble method involves two types of models: base-level models and a meta-level model.
The base-level models include ECCNN, Roost, and Magpie, denoted as f 1, f 2, and f 3. The meta-level model is a multi-response linear regression (MLR), denoted as F.
The training of the meta-level model requires a five-fold split of the training set... For each base model, we iteratively train on four folds and predict on the remaining fold...

stages.stage_name_raw: Benchmarking ECSG against state-of-the-art models using multiple metrics
stages.stage_goal: Quantitatively assess predictive performance using AUC, ACC, Precision, Recall, F1, NPV, AUPR across multiple datasets
stage_input: test sets from MP, OQMD, JARVIS, perovskite halides, Li-oxides, transition metal oxides

evidence.text: In this section, we performed a comprehensive comparison between our proposed method and several state-of-the-art baselines... to validate the effectiveness of our proposed ECSG.

We include several metrics, Area Under the receiver operating characteristic Curve (AUC), accuracy (ACC), Precision, Recall, F1-score (F1), negative predictive values (NPV), and Area Under the Precision-Recall curve (AUPR), to provide a more comprehensive evaluation.

stages.stage_name_raw: Ablation study to quantify contribution of each base model and stacking strategy
stages.stage_goal: Isolate the performance impact of removing individual base models (ECCNN, Roost, Magpie) or replacing stacked generalization with voting/averaging
stage_output: Supplementary Table 7 (SG vs. averaging vs. voting)

evidence.text: To comprehend the individual contributions of each base model of ECSG to its performance improvement, we tested the performance of each base model after removing it from ECSG.

SG performs the best, followed by averaging, while voting lags behind. For example, compared to averaging, SG improves ACC, F1, and AUC from 0.788, 0.719, and 0.865 to 0.807, 0.752, and 0.886, respectively.

stages.stage_name_raw: Screening candidate materials in unexplored composition space (e.g., perovskites, 2D materials)
stages.stage_goal: Apply trained ECSG to rank millions of hypothetical compounds by predicted stability probability and select high-confidence candidates for validation
stage_output: ranked list of stable candidates (e.g., 1,877,443 perovskite oxides with p > 0.5)

evidence.text: We constructed the candidate space of perovskites by enumerating all possible ABO3, A2BB′O6, AA′B2O6, and AA′BB′O6 compounds... resulting in 4,524,608 unique compounds, forming the candidate composition space.
Subsequently, we utilized the trained super learner to predict the stability of all perovskite oxides within this space.
By setting the cutoff probability to 0.5, we identiﬁed 1,877,443 perovskite oxides predicted to be stable, substantially narrowing down our search range.

stages.stage_name_raw: Validating predictions via first-principles DFT calculations
stages.stage_goal: Confirm predicted stability of top-ranked candidates using density functional theory (DFT) to compute formation energies and construct convex hulls

evidence.text: We randomly selected 35 compounds with stability probabilities greater than 90% (63 in total) for ﬁrst-principles calculations to validate the accuracy of our machine-learning method.

The total energy calculations in this study were performed using the DFT framework as implemented in the Vienna ab initio simulation package (VASP)... To construct the convex hull for each set of elements comprising A-A′-B-B′-O, the total energy data of all compounds in the MP database was considered and extracted using the database API.
